                    ### Question
                    Indicate the clinical situation that, in relation to infection with hepatitis B virus, presents a 5-year-old patient from Nigeria, with normal physical examination and with the following serology against hepatitis B: HBsAg + / ANTI-HBs - / HbeAg - / ANTI-HBe + / / ANTI-HBc IgM - / ANTI-HBc IgG + / DNA HBV +:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acute infection
opb. Chronic infection
opc. Vaccinated patient.
opd. Asymptomatic carrier

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The 5-year-old patient from Nigeria with HBsAg+, ANTI-HBs-, HbeAg-, ANTI-HBe+, ANTI-HBc IgM-, ANTI-HBc IgG+, and DNA HBV+ serology likely indicates acute hepatitis B infection rather than chronic infection, vaccination, or asymptomatic carrier status. The presence of HBsAg suggests active infection, supported by the absence of ANTI-HBs and presence of DNA HBV indicating active viral replication. The presence of ANTI-HBe and absence of ANTI-HBc IgM suggest an immune response to the virus and lower likelihood of chronic infection. The evidence paths do not significantly impact this interpretation.
